title: Case and declension
about: Greek marks a noun's job with its ending and its article: nominative for the subject and after *είμαι*, accusative for the object and after almost every preposition, genitive for possession and for the person you give or say something to, vocative when you call someone. Most slips come from leaving a noun in the nominative because that is the form in the dictionary.

items.en: I give my friend a present.

errs.why: The person you give something to is the indirect object: *σε* + accusative (*στον φίλο μου*) or the genitive (*του φίλου μου*), never the nominative.

items.en: I'm going to the cinema with my sister.

errs.why: *με* takes the accusative: *με την αδελφή μου*, *με τον αδελφό μου*.

items.en: This is Maria's house.

errs.why: Possession is the genitive: *της Μαρίας*, *του Νίκου*. The genitive follows the noun it belongs to.

items.en: On Monday I work until five.

errs.why: "On Monday" is a time expression in the accusative without a preposition: *τη Δευτέρα*, *το Σάββατο*, *την Κυριακή*.

items.en: Good morning, Mr Papadopoulos!

errs.why: When you speak to someone you use the vocative: masculine *-ος* becomes *-ε* (*κύριε Παπαδόπουλε*), *-ης* drops the *ς* (*Γιάννη*).

items.en: My sister is a doctor.

errs.why: After *είμαι* the noun describing the subject stays in the nominative: *είναι γιατρός*. *γιατρός* is the same word for a man and a woman.

parts: Το βράδυ τρώμε με τους γονείς της Ελένης.
items.en: In the evening we eat with Eleni's parents.
items.why: Nothing to fix: *το βράδυ* (time, accusative), *με τους γονείς* (accusative after *με*), *της Ελένης* (genitive of possession).

items.en: I told him to come early.

errs.why: The person you tell something to takes the genitive clitic: *του είπα*, *της είπα*. *Τον είπα* is heard in northern Greece but is not standard.

items.en: I'm thirty (years old).

errs.why: Age is *είμαι* + number + genitive: *είμαι τριάντα χρονών* (everyday) or *τριάντα χρόνων*; formal *ετών*. *Είμαι τριάντα χρόνια* is a calque of English.

items.en: The pupils' parents came to the meeting.

errs.why: Genitive plural always ends in *-ων*: *των μαθητών*, *των φίλων*, *των πόλεων*.

items.en: We lost the car keys.

errs.why: Neuter nouns in *-ο* stressed on the third syllable from the end move the stress in the genitive: *το αυτοκίνητο*, *του αυτοκινήτου*, *των αυτοκινήτων*.

items.en: Nikos showed us all our mistakes.

errs.why: *το λάθος* is a neuter noun in *-ος*: plural *τα λάθη*, genitive *του λάθους*, *των λαθών*. Same pattern: *το μέρος* → *τα μέρη*, *το δάσος* → *τα δάση*.

items.en: We spent the evening at my uncle's house.

errs.why: "My uncle's" is the genitive: *του θείου μου*. A noun that belongs to another noun never stays in the nominative.

parts: Έστειλα στη γιαγιά μου μια κάρτα για τη γιορτή της.
items.en: I sent my grandmother a card for her name day.
items.why: Nothing to fix: *σε* + accusative for the person who receives (*στη γιαγιά μου*), *για* + accusative (*για τη γιορτή της*).

items.en: The flight was cancelled because of the bad weather.

errs.why: *λόγω* "because of" and *εξαιτίας* take the genitive: *λόγω της κακοκαιρίας*, *εξαιτίας της απεργίας*.

items.en: We went out despite the rain.

errs.why: *παρά* "despite" takes the accusative: *παρά τη βροχή*, *παρά τις δυσκολίες*.

items.en: The girl I met yesterday is Italian.

errs.why: *ο οποίος* takes the case of its job inside its own clause. Here it is the object of *γνώρισα*, so accusative: *την οποία γνώρισα*.

items.en: Many writers from Cyprus came to the festival.

errs.why: *ο συγγραφέας* has the plural *οι συγγραφείς*, *των συγγραφέων*, *τους συγγραφείς*; genitive singular *του συγγραφέα*. Same pattern: *ο γραμματέας* → *οι γραμματείς*.

items.en: The success of the method depends on the teacher.

errs.why: *η μέθοδος* is feminine but declines like *ο άνθρωπος*: genitive *της μεθόδου*, plural *οι μέθοδοι*. So do *η οδός*, *η είσοδος*, *η έξοδος*, *η περίοδος*.

items.en: We have two daughters and a son.

errs.why: After *έχω* the object is accusative: *έναν γιο* (nominative *ένας γιος*). *Δύο κόρες* is already right, because feminine nouns in *-η/-α* have the same form for nominative and accusative plural.

parts: Μετά από τόσα χρόνια, θυμάμαι ακόμα τη φωνή της δασκάλας μου.
items.en: After so many years I still remember my teacher's voice.
items.why: Nothing to fix: *μετά από* + accusative, *τη φωνή* (object), *της δασκάλας μου* (genitive of possession).

items.en: During the crisis many young people left for abroad.

errs.why: *κατά τη διάρκεια* "during" is followed by the genitive: *της κρίσης* (learned *της κρίσεως* is also correct in formal texts). Feminine nouns in *-η* add *-ς* in the genitive singular.

items.en: The decisions were taken on the basis of the 2019 law.

errs.why: *βάσει* "on the basis of" is a learned preposition with the genitive: *βάσει του νόμου*. Its everyday equivalent *με βάση* takes the accusative: *με βάση τον νόμο*.

items.en: The protest was aimed against the government.

errs.why: *εναντίον* takes the genitive (*εναντίον της κυβέρνησης*); the everyday *ενάντια* takes *σε* (*ενάντια στην κυβέρνηση*). Mixing the two is a common slip.

items.en: The text was signed on behalf of the director.

errs.why: *εκ μέρους* "on behalf of" is followed by the genitive: *εκ μέρους του διευθυντή*.

items.en: Cooperation between the two countries is close.

errs.why: *μεταξύ* takes the genitive: *μεταξύ των δύο χωρών*. Everyday *ανάμεσα σε* takes the accusative: *ανάμεσα στις δύο χώρες*.

parts: Ήταν ένας από τους πιο σημαντικούς
items.en: He was one of the most important researchers of his generation.

errs.why: After *ένας από τους* the noun is accusative plural, agreeing with *τους*: *τους πιο σημαντικούς ερευνητές*.
